text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fundamentalists have shed scruples in their terror attacks. Working-class districts were those most targeted by bombers. But despite this suffering, Algerians pursue their daily life with courage.
- More than 60 people killed in Medea.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and CNT speaker Abdelkader Bensalah attend burial service in memory of Ali Hamdi, junior planning minister, who shot himself dead while he was cleaning his gun.
- Workers's union officials and state-owned company managers negotiate salaries.
- Algiers car bomb toll rises to more than 40.
- More than 700,000 families benefit from state-funded safety net for poor.
- Following bomb attacks and village raids, many citizens asked the source of the explosives used in bombings.
- Opposition parties, Socialist Forces Front (FFS) and Islamist Nahda call on the authorities to change rules governing an election watchdog body.
